import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import norm

def task_func(df, column, bins=30, density=True, alpha=0.6, color="g", seed=None):
    if seed is not None:
        np.random.seed(seed)

    data = df[column].dropna().to_numpy()

    fig, ax = plt.subplots()

    # Plot histogram
    ax.hist(data, bins=bins, density=density, alpha=alpha, color=color)

    # Fit and overlay normal distribution curve
    mu, sigma = norm.fit(data)
    if data.size > 0:
        x_min, x_max = np.min(data), np.max(data)
        if x_min == x_max:
            x_min -= 1.0
            x_max += 1.0
        x = np.linspace(x_min, x_max, 200)
        if sigma > 0:
            y = norm.pdf(x, mu, sigma)
        else:
            y = np.zeros_like(x)
            y[np.argmin(np.abs(x - mu))] = 1.0
        ax.plot(x, y, "r-", linewidth=2)

    ax.set_title(f"Histogram of {column} with fitted normal distribution")
    ax.set_xlabel(column)
    ax.set_ylabel("Density" if density else "Count")

    return ax
